core_obligations: (2) ⇒ (1): compute E ⊗^L F = E^• ⊗ F, which has cohomology only in [a,b] (proof lines 12362-12367).

(1) ⇒ (2): represent E by a bounded above complex of flat modules K^•; induct on the top degree n > b: K^{n-1} → K^n is surjective with flat kernel (Modules, Lemma flat-ses), so replace K^• by τ_{≤n-1}K^• (proof lines 12368-12383).
Set E^• = τ_{≥a}K^•; everything is clear except flatness of E^a, which follows from the last-one-flat lemma (proof lines 12384-12387).
proof_roadmap: Shave the resolution down to the range by induction.
Flatness of the bottom term from last-one-flat.
difficulty_reason: (2) implies (1) by direct computation; for the converse the proof inducts on the top degree of a bounded above flat resolution, using flatness of kernels, and the final flatness of the bottom term comes from the last-one-flat lemma.
